data.title: Overflow
data.tagline: Overflow is the rule for how the browser shows, clips, or scrolls content that exceeds a container's available space.
data.learningOutcome: You can locate the overflowing container, choose growth, wrapping, scrolling, or intentional clipping, and verify that essential information and actions remain reachable.
data.description: When a card has a fixed height, longer content can cross its bottom edge. If an ancestor uses `overflow: hidden`, the bottom description and action disappear. Overflow can be horizontal or vertical. It answers what happens after content no longer fits and should not hide a layout that needs reworking.

learning.assumes: You have seen a missing card bottom, overflowing text, a scrollable table, or a cropped image.
learning.outcome: You can locate the overflowing container, choose growth, wrapping, scrolling, or intentional clipping, and verify that essential information and actions remain reachable.

explanation.title: Find which layer no longer fits
explanation.text: First check whether content crosses the card boundary, then inspect the exact container's fixed `height`, `max-height`, `overflow`, and real scroll area. `hidden` only conceals the result; it does not explain why content no longer fits.

explanation.title: Essential content must remain visible or reachable
explanation.text: A normal content card should usually grow with its content. Use internal scrolling only for intentionally bounded lists or panels, with a visible cue. Do not silently clip an action, error, or primary content.

data.boundary: Overflow is neither responsive design nor every kind of visual obstruction. If content stays inside its boundary but a fixed bar, absolutely positioned element, or another layer covers it, inspect positioning and stacking. Handle overflow when content actually crosses the container boundary; do not blindly hide it or raise `z-index`.

lessonPractice.title: A content card loses its Download video button when the copy becomes longer. What is the best first step?

options.label: Find the exact container with a fixed height or `overflow: hidden`, then choose whether the card should grow or, only when bounded height is intentional, scroll internally
options.feedback: Correct. Identify the vertical overflow layer first, then choose growth or scrolling so the bottom action stays reachable.

options.label: Only set the button's `z-index` to 9999 without checking whether its parent clips it
options.feedback: Content clipped by a parent normally does not reappear merely because its own stacking level increases. Inspect the boundary, height, and overflow first.

options.label: Delete the last description so this one card happens to fit
options.feedback: Real content length changes. Removing content only avoids this instance and does not prove the card handles the longest case.

data.agentPrompt: Inspect this card's vertical overflow and identify the exact container using a fixed height, `max-height`, or `overflow: hidden`. The title, descriptions, and bottom action must remain visible and operable. Prefer letting a normal content card grow; use internal scrolling only when bounded height is intentional. Test the longest content on desktop and at 390px.
